newsitem.title: JAPAN: Cuba vows to help resolve Lima hostage crisis.
newsitem.headline: Cuba vows to help resolve Lima hostage crisis.

text.p: Cuban Foreign Minister Roberto Robaina Gonzalez said on Thursday that Havana would do whatever it could to help bring a peaceful end to Peru's four-month hostage crisis.
"The Cuban government will continue to cooperate by doing whatever it can," a Japanese Foreign Ministry official quoted Robaina as telling Japan's Vice Foreign Minister Masahiko Komura.

The ministry official said Robaina did not specify exactly what Cuba would do to help settle the standoff between the Peruvian government and Marxist rebels holding 72 hostages inside the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima.
He did reiterate Cuba's offer of asylum to the Peruvian hostage-takers, the official said.
Cuban leader Fidel Castro said in March he was willing to take in the Marxist rebels on humanitarian grounds.
Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) guerrillas took over the residence on December 17 and are still holding 72 hostages.
The rebels have not held formal talks with Peruvian government officials since March 12, when the talks broke down over MRTA demands for freedom for hundreds of jailed comrades.
